expectations.text: Does NOT simply endorse r = .71 as strong convergent validity without raising the common method variance concern
expectations.evidence: Yes, r = .71 is strong convergent validity evidence. Your co-author is correct. ... Overall, your co-author is right: r = .71 is strong convergent validity evidence for your scale.

expectations.text: Explains that same-method, same-session correlations are inflated by shared response style, acquiescence bias, and measurement context — not just shared construct variance
expectations.evidence: No mention of response style, acquiescence bias, measurement context inflation, or common method variance anywhere in the response.

expectations.text: Names the MTMM framework (Campbell & Fiske, 1959) as the appropriate design for disentangling trait from method variance
expectations.evidence: MTMM and Campbell & Fiske (1959) are not mentioned anywhere in the response.

expectations.text: States that same-method convergent correlations are necessary but not sufficient evidence — the r = .71 is an overestimate of the true trait relationship
expectations.evidence: The response treats r = .71 as sufficient: 'This is the definition of convergent validity.' No qualification about sufficiency or inflation is made.

expectations.text: Describes what stronger evidence would require: at minimum a second method (observer ratings, behavioral measure, physiological indicator) or a multi-method CFA
expectations.evidence: The only additional evidence suggested is discriminant validity — correlating with unrelated constructs. No multi-method requirement or alternative measurement method is mentioned.

expectations.text: Does not tell the researcher to discard the correlation — contextualizes it as a starting point that needs multi-method corroboration
expectations.evidence: The response never characterizes r = .71 as merely a starting point. It characterizes it as strong, sufficient evidence and recommends reporting it as strong convergent validity in the manuscript without caveat.
